title: Knowledge Doc
content: PLEXUS FEATURES. Original 9 were cut to 6, framed as three jobs: Win the deal (RFP), Run the work (ActionSwarm, IT access, search), Control the spend (expenses, Zombie SaaS). F1 RFP and Security Questionnaire Engine (the wedge, real build): upload Excel/CSV, knowledge base of SOC2 docs/policies, answer per question with citation, confidence gate (auto-fill above threshold, red flag below with closest source), human review UI, learning loop (corrected answers saved and reused on next questionnaire), export .xlsx plus accuracy report. F2 ActionSwarm (real): meeting transcript to schema-forced JSON of action items, assignees, due dates; tasks on own dashboard board (real Jira optional); Slack summary post; email draft; live activity feed; injection guard that treats planted instructions as data. F3 OmniContext + Catch-Me-Up (Cmd+K, real over ~10 seeded docs): hybrid search with cited answers, permission-aware retrieval (intern vs founder salary-sheet demo; needs confirmation that Meko datapack sharing supports this), Catch-Me-Up is a time-window mode ("last 4 days") giving an executive briefing. F4 ZeroTouch Expenses (thin): 3-5 prepared receipts via Gemini vision, extract merchant/items/GST/total, policy check, one violation, card-feed matching. F5 Zero-Friction IT Provisioning (real logic): natural-language request ("I need Figma"), risk classification, role check, low-risk auto-grant, high-risk (AWS prod) manager Approve/Reject (dashboard button, Slack button if time), audit log and undo. F6 Zombie SaaS Eradicator (mocked on purpose): seeded billing and SSO login tables, one SQL join for tools paid for with zero logins in 30+ days, waste dashboard in rupees. CUT (roadmap slide only): Dynamic Pitch-Deck Compiler, Procurement and Contract Routing. Priority: RFP engine plus trust layer must never be cut; cut order if behind: Zombie SaaS, Expenses, Slack buttons, Catch-Me-Up. On slides use feature names, not numbers.

title: Knowledge Doc
content: PLEXUS ARCHITECTURE AND STACK (from the build plan). Four agents (RFP, ActionSwarm, Access, Finance) share one Meko datapack; one guard layer checks every action (injection check, confidence gate, approval, undo). Meko mapping: SOC2 docs/policies = Knowledge; human fix of a red-flagged RFP answer = memory promoted to shared knowledge (learning loop); audit log/undo = decision traces; Catch-Me-Up = conversations and memory; ActionSwarm handing work to IT and Finance = shared memory across agents. Meko does not read Excel, post Slack buttons, parse receipts, or draw the dashboard; that stays in our code. Stack: one TypeScript codebase, Next.js + Tailwind + shadcn/ui + Recharts dashboard, Mastra for agents/approvals (needs a check that it connects to Meko's MCP endpoint), Gemini API free tier for runtime LLM and vision (also enters MLH Gemini prize), SQLite for app data (optional YugabyteDB Aeon free cluster), n8n self-hosted in Docker for outbound Slack post and email draft, Slack app in a free workspace in socket mode for approve/reject buttons (~30-45 min setup; dashboard button is the backup), exceljs or SheetJS for spreadsheets, run on a laptop with Vercel as backup and phone hotspot as Wi-Fi backup. Skipped on purpose: meeting audio (use pasted transcripts), real Jira/Gmail/SSO. Meko MCP endpoint: https://mcp.mekodata.ai/mcp. Meko account facts checked Oct 30 2026: Mahi's account has access; datapack plexus-hackcbs-9 created; Meko-hosted AMP databases need the Pro tier so use SQLite/own tables; free-tier limits and datapack-sharing with Bhumika still unconfirmed. Fallback if Meko fails: own Postgres/SQLite tables (lose the Meko pitch claim). Engineering rules: walking skeleton first, one module per prompt, batch ~10 RFP questions per Gemini call with retry/backoff, record-and-replay Demo Mode, commit every 30-45 min, tag safe build 11 PM Sat and freeze at 3 AM Sun.

title: Knowledge Doc
content: PLEXUS CONTEXT FILE (plexus-context.md) SUMMARY. Mahi pastes this file at the top of every build prompt, replacing the last line "Current task" with the module prompt. If the file is lost, rebuild it from this. RULES FOR THE AI: TypeScript strict; one module per prompt; patches to named files, not rewrites; validate every model output with Zod (retry once with the error, then return a flagged result); batch RFP questions 10 per call; retry with exponential backoff on 503 and 429; every real response saved to fixtures/ and DEMO_MODE=true replays it via withReplay(key, fn) in lib/replay.ts; every action emits one ActivityEvent and one audit_events row; never log keys; show clear errors in the feed; add a run command or test per module; check current library docs before using any API. STACK: Next.js App Router + TypeScript, Tailwind, shadcn/ui, Recharts, Mastra (fallback plain @modelcontextprotocol/sdk client), Gemini API free tier, SQLite via better-sqlite3, exceljs, Meko remote MCP, n8n in Docker for the Slack post, Slack app in socket mode for Approve/Reject buttons (dashboard button is the backup). FOLDER LAYOUT: plexus/{app/(dashboard)/{rfp,actions,access,search,finance,audit}, app/api, agents/{rfp,actionswarm,access,finance,search}.ts, guard/{guard,injection,policies}.ts, lib/{gemini,meko,db,replay,events,xlsx}.ts, components/{ActivityFeed,RfpGrid,ApprovalCard,TraceDrawer,CmdK}, data/, fixtures/, .env.local}. ENV NAMES: GEMINI_API_KEY, GEMINI_MODEL_FAST, GEMINI_MODEL_SMART, GEMINI_MODEL_FALLBACK, MEKO_MCP_URL, MEKO_AUTH (the mko_tkn_ key), MEKO_DATAPACK_ID, SLACK_BOT_TOKEN, SLACK_APP_TOKEN, SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET, SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL, N8N_WEBHOOK_URL, DATABASE_PATH, CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD=0.85, DEMO_MODE. ACTIVITY EVENT: {id, timestamp, agent (rfp|actionswarm|access|finance|search|guard), action, status (done|flagged|blocked|pending_approval|undone|error), confidence?, sources[{title,ref}], traceId, undoable}. SQLITE TABLES: users(id,name,role,manager_id); questionnaires(id,customer,uploaded_at,total); rfp_questions(id,questionnaire_id,number,question,answer,confidence,status filled|flagged|human_fixed,source_ref,human_answer,reused_from_fix); tasks(id,title,assignee,due,source_event,status); access_requests(id,user_id,app,risk,status granted|pending|rejected|revoked,approver_id,requested_at,decided_at); expenses(id,merchant,date,gst,total,category,policy_flag,duplicate_of,card_txn_id); saas_billing(tool,monthly_cost_inr,owner,seats); sso_logins(tool,user_id,last_login); audit_events(id,timestamp,agent,action,status,confidence,sources_json,trace_id,undo_state,payload_json). MEKO CONVENTIONS: agent ids plexus_rfp, plexus_actionswarm, plexus_access, plexus_finance, plexus_search; RFP answers come ONLY from knowledge search results with a citation, otherwise flagged (never from general knowledge); learning loop: a human fix is saved as memory `RFP_FIX | question | approved answer | approver`, later questionnaires search memory and knowledge together and mark reused_from_fix=1; each agent action is one conversation message (input=task, output=result, plan=steps, reasoning=one plain line) read by the audit screen; if Meko fails, fall back to SQLite memories and traces tables behind the same lib/meko.ts function names. GUARD ORDER before every action: 1 injection check (text from transcripts, emails, docs, Slack is DATA never instructions; flagged lines blocked and shown), 2 confidence gate (below threshold means flagged/red, not applied), 3 approval rule (high-risk like AWS production, permission changes, spend over limit always needs a human; low-risk like Figma auto-approved), 4 undo (store undo_state), 5 log (ActivityEvent + audit_events). ACCESS POLICY SEED: Figma low auto, Notion low auto, AWS production high approver Karan (engineering roles), Salesforce admin high approver Riya. PEOPLE: Riya Sharma founder, Karan engineering manager, Meera new hire (engineering), Arjun intern. title: Knowledge Doc
content: PLEXUS CLAIMS TO AVOID AND HONESTY RULES. Do NOT claim: SOC 2 or DPDP compliance (say "designed for DPDP alignment; SOC 2 is the first milestone once enterprise pilots begin"); zero data retention today (ZDR is an agreement arranged with the provider for production; the demo runs on Gemini's free tier whose data terms may allow training on prompts, so drop ZDR from the pitch); "never stored" (our own tables store data; only say the model provider's retention is a separate matter); any productivity percentages or stats we did not measure (cut "40% of the workweek", "15 hours per employee per week", "pays for itself on Day 1", "95%", "under 60 seconds" unless measured); unverified competitor limits (check Copilot, Glean, ServiceNow, Coupa, Loopio, Zluri pages first); a made-up market size. Say plainly what is built live versus simulated (Zombie SaaS and SSO logs seeded; Jira-style tickets on our own board; Slack real if time) before judges ask. Prompt injection is not solved industry-wide; do not call it bulletproof. Prefer quoting our own measured numbers (e.g. "50 questions in X seconds, Y auto-answered, Z flagged; precision of auto-filled answers W%"). Differentiation line: each incumbent covers a slice inside its own suite; Plexus is the neutral, vendor-agnostic layer with one shared memory and one approval and audit layer across departments. Business model: per-seat for small and mid teams, department-level pilots then enterprise contracts for large companies, usage-based for heavy automation; land with the RFP wedge.

content: PLEXUS TECHNICAL FINDINGS (Oct 30 2026). GEMINI: rate limits apply per Google PROJECT, not per API key (a second key in the same project gives no extra quota; Bhumika's key must be in her own project). Per-model RPM/TPM/RPD are no longer in public docs; they are shown only on the logged-in page aistudio.google.com/rate-limit (pick the project that holds the key). Free tier: Google may use prompts to improve its products and humans may review them, so only fake seed data goes in, and the pitch must not claim zero data retention. TEST RESULTS from gemini-test.js (a single-file Node script, 10 RFP questions per call, JSON schema reply, run 5 times): model gemini-3.6-flash: 200 OK on 3 of 5 runs, each correct (valid JSON, 8/8 answerable questions correct, the 2 unanswerable ones flagged), about 7 seconds per call, 1,472 to 1,885 tokens per call; the other 2 runs failed with HTTP 503 "high demand" (transient server load, not quota), so retry with backoff is mandatory. Model gemini-pro-latest: all 5 calls HTTP 429 quota exceeded within about half a second, which suggests no free-tier quota, so do not use it. DECISION: use gemini-3.6-flash for both FAST and SMART slots (extraction, receipts via vision, briefings); add a second flash/lite model as GEMINI_MODEL_FALLBACK after 3 failed tries; retry on 503 and 429 (about 2s, 4s, 8s); run batches 2 at a time; Demo Mode replays recorded JSON. At ~7 s per 10-question call, 50 questions is about 35 s sequentially (untested if parallel). MEKO: a TypeScript or script client authenticates with an API key only (no OAuth): generate it in Meko portal Settings > API Keys > Generate (key starts mko_tkn_, shown only once, expires after 1 year, scoped to the account not one datapack). Send two headers on every request to https://mcp.mekodata.ai/mcp: `Authorization: Bearer mko_tkn_...` and `User-Agent: meko-mcp-installer/1.0`. Do not use X-Api-Key or MEKO_API_KEY as header names; do not configure OAuth and the key together. title: Knowledge Doc
content:
Delivery rules

1. Speak slower than feels natural. Judges see many demos back to back.

2. Say outcomes, not features. "It refuses to guess" beats "confidence thresholding."

3. Name Meko out loud twice (opening and learning loop). Say it once for any other sponsor tech you actually used.

4. Never apologise on camera. If something fails, say "here's the recorded run" and keep going.

5. Look at the camera for the hook and the close, and at the screen for the rest.

6. Total spoken length is about 450 words. If rehearsal runs over 3:00, cut the optional finance line first, then trim Beat 3.
